title: Mango Sticky Rice
subtitle: sweet glutinous rice with ripe mango and coconut cream
excerpt: Thailand's most beloved dessert. Warm sweet rice with cold ripe mango and salted coconut cream. Serves four.
sourceNotes: A classic Thai dessert, especially popular in the mango season from March to June.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook and season the rice up to 2 hours ahead. Keep covered at room temperature. Slice mango just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: Also called sticky rice or sweet rice. A short-grain rice that becomes dense and chewy when steamed. It must be soaked before cooking.
Pressed liquid from grated coconut flesh. Used here to season the rice and make the topping sauce.

content.text: Mango sticky rice serves 4 and takes about 40 minutes including soaking. The dish centres on
while still hot, then served alongside sliced ripe mango and a second pour of salted coconut cream. Use the ripest, most fragrant mango you can find.
Soak the glutinous rice for at least 4 hours before steaming. Overnight soaking gives the most even, tender result.

items.prepNote: soaked in cold water 4 hours or overnight

content.text: Drain the soaked glutinous rice. Steam over boiling water in a lined steamer basket for 20 to 25 minutes until tender and translucent.
While the rice steams, heat 250 ml of the coconut milk in a saucepan with the {{palm-sugar}} and a pinch of salt over medium heat. Stir until dissolved. Do not boil. Set aside.
Transfer the hot rice to a bowl. Pour the sweetened coconut milk mixture over it. Stir gently and cover. Leave to absorb for 10 minutes. The rice will thicken and become glossy.
For the topping sauce, heat the remaining 150 ml coconut milk with the {{caster-sugar}} and a good pinch of salt. Stir until dissolved. This sauce should taste slightly salty-sweet.
Peel 2 ripe mangoes and slice the flesh away from the stone in long strips. Arrange neatly on plates.
Spoon the sticky rice alongside the mango. Drizzle the salted coconut topping sauce over the rice. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Rice is still hard after steaming
items.cause: Under-soaked or steamer lid lifted too often
items.fix: Steam for 5 more minutes with the lid firmly on. Always soak rice a full 4 hours.

items.cause: Too much coconut milk absorbed, or rice over-soaked
items.fix: Next time reduce the coconut milk to 200 ml. Let it absorb fully before adding more.

items.cause: Too much palm sugar in the topping
items.fix: The topping sauce should be salty first, sweet second. Add an extra pinch of salt to balance.

content.text: Mango sticky rice is one of the most recognised Thai desserts outside Thailand. It is sold from carts and market stalls throughout the country, particularly during the mango season from spring into early summer. The Nam Dok Mai mango, pale yellow and intensely fragrant, is the traditional variety. Any very ripe, sweet mango works well. The contrast between the warm, dense rice and the cool, juicy mango is the whole point of the dish.
